editorial.headline: Grape Farming With a Clear Bali Registration Path
editorial.standfirst: Grape cultivation is open to foreign ownership nationally and, on this record, is not stopped by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Grape farming under this activity is first of all an agricultural registration, not a beverage or food-processing licence. Its centre of gravity is the vineyard itself: preparing the land, planting vines, maintaining the crop, harvesting grapes, and carrying out post-harvest work when that work is part of the same farming sequence. The record is broad enough to include grapes grown for direct consumption and grapes grown as raw material for wine, juice, vinegar, raisins, zante currants, and sultanas. It also includes grape planting aimed at producing seed.

That makes the code useful for founders whose real business asset is cultivation: land preparation, vine management, harvest discipline, and integrated post-harvest handling. The boundary matters. The slim record expressly keeps winemaking outside this activity, and it also excludes grape processing and preservation. A company should therefore not treat this registration as a catch-all for everything that may happen after grapes leave the farming chain. Its editorial meaning is narrower and cleaner: this is the code for growing grapes and managing the immediate agricultural cycle around them.

The scale picture is unusually open. The record lists Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar as open scales, so the activity is not framed only for a large estate or only for a small local farm. It can describe anything from a smaller cultivation operation to a larger farming business, provided the registered activity remains grape agriculture. Nationally, the investment field is also clear: the PMA status is TERBUKA, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. There is no partial cap in the record, so the honest national reading is that a foreign-owned company can use this activity at full foreign ownership, subject only to the facts stated here.

The Bali question is where this record becomes especially important. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the province, but this activity is not marked as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason that OSS risk at Besar is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. In practical editorial terms: a foreigner is not barred by the Bali moratorium from registering this grape-farming activity today. That does not create extra permissions beyond the record, and it does not turn farming into processing. It simply means the national openness and the Bali registration position point in the same direction here: grape cultivation, at the stated scales, is a viable PMA registration path in Bali on this record.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreigner is not barred by the Bali moratorium from registering this grape-farming activity today.
